stem: Meera's class sets up a pit behind the school garden where vegetable peels, fallen leaves and cow dung are buried for several weeks. Later, the material has turned into dark, crumbly manure. What best explains how this change happened?

options.text: Soil fungi and bacteria slowly broke down the plant and animal waste into simpler, nutrient-rich manure.
The peels and dung dried out in the pit and turned into manure on their own.
The buried waste attracted microorganisms, which then fed on the ready-made manure.
Microorganisms need plenty of open air and sunlight to change the waste into manure.

teacher.key_rationale: Decomposition is carried out by soil microorganisms (fungi and bacteria) acting on plant and animal waste, converting it into simpler nutrient-rich manure; B omits the role of microbes, C reverses the causal relationship, and D states a false condition since decomposition in a covered pit does not require open air and sunlight.
